correctness.rationale: The exact effective-potential derivative is (μλ/r³)(H_α−p). Its derivative at a circular orbit has the sign of H′_α=1−αg, where g′(x)=x(3−x)e^(−x). The unique positive maximum g(3)=5e^(−3) gives α_c=e³/5 and the signs +,−,+ above it, with two simple folds and the claimed global one/two/three-root census from H_α(0+)=0 and H_α(∞)=∞. A fold is a stationary inflection of the radial potential, not a quartic minimum. Simultaneous vanishing of H′ and H″ occurs only at x=3, p=27/5; H‴=3/5 gives U(r_c+z)−U(r_c)=a z⁴+O(|z|⁵), a=μ/(1080λ⁵)>0. For the period, write y=z[(U(r_c+z)−U(r_c))/(a z⁴)]^(1/4), an analytic local coordinate with derivative 1 at 0. For energy at the outer turn A, y runs between ±y(A). Its inverse derivative tends uniformly to 1 after scaling y by y(A), and (1−u⁴)^(-1/2) is integrable on [−1,1]. The full out-and-back integral therefore gives AT→B(1/4,1/2)/sqrt(2a), with no turning-point uniformity assumption needed. Across the excursion the angular rate tends uniformly to sqrt(μ/(15λ³)) in the positive orientation (the swept magnitude is unchanged by reversing orientation), giving (A/λ)Δθ→6B(1/4,1/2). H′_(α_c(1+η))(3+δ)=−η+3δ²/10+O(|δ|³+ηδ²) yields δ_±=±sqrt(10η/3)+O(η); integrating from zero to these roots gives opposite shifts of magnitude (2/3)sqrt(10/3)η^(3/2) about the common center p_c+12η/5, with the correct fold-label reversal. Separate symbolic and quadrature diagnostics agree: with μ=λ=1 the period and angle ratios to the stated laws are 1.00537 and 1.00534 at A=0.02; the fold width divided by η^(3/2) is 2.43424 at η=10^(-4) versus 2.43432248 in the limit.
